_note: How to say Euskara out loud, for an English speaker standing at a bar. Written by this project and NOT reviewed by a Basque speaker — same caveat as the interface strings in eu.json.

letters.like: the same, but softer — tongue tip higher
a sharp s — never a z
a whistlier s, tongue tip up
y in the north, a throaty h in Bizkaia and in Spanish-influenced speech
as in canyon; -in- often does the same
silent in the south, breathed in the north
hard, always — never the g in gem
pure, every time, as in Spanish or Italian

rules: Vowels never slide. Basque has five and they keep their value wherever they fall.
Stress is light. Nobody will misunderstand you for putting it in the wrong place; the second syllable is a safe guess.
A final -a is often the word for "the": ogi is bread, ogia is the bread, sagardo is cider, sagardoa is the cider.
Euskara is related to no other living language. There is nothing to transfer from Spanish or French, which is why the spelling looks stranger than it sounds.
